newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Sega, Bandai cancel merger plans.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Sega, Bandai cancel merger plans.

text.p: Japan's Sega Enterprises Ltd said on Tuesday it had accepted Bandai Co Ltd's request to cancel their planned merger, which would have created the nation's largest game company.
"Bandai requested a cancellation of the merger and offered a business alliance instead, which we accepted," a Sega spokeswoman told Reuters.

The surprise announcement came only a day before the two firms were due to approve a merger pact, slated to take effect on October 1, and a day after toymaker Bandai had called a news conference to confirm it was still on board with the merger.

Sega, maker of the Sega Saturn 32-bit video-game player, and Bandai, known for its Power Rangers and virtual pet toy "Tamagotchi", said in January that they would merge to create a global entertainment giant likened to Walt Disney Co.

The spokeswoman did not give a reason for the break-up, but speculation had already grown prior to the announcement that the merger could be delayed due to strong opposition from mid-level managers at Bandai.

On Monday, a Bandai executive called a sudden news conference to say that the company expected its board to approve the merger with Sega at a meeting on Wednesday, withdrawing an earlier plan to postpone approval until July.

Bandai managing director Mikio Ishigami told reporters that employees at the toymaker were "extremely nervous" about the change of environment, but that he was confident they would come on board once the blueprint for the merged company became clear.

Analysts said the cancellation announcement, which came after the Tokyo stock market closed, would be negative for the two firms, although they were split over which firm had more to lose from the failed deal.

"They had repeatedly said that there would be no future without a merger. The cancellation would be taken as negative, especially for Bandai," said Yasuo Imanaka, an analyst at Okasan Economic Research Institute. "Bandai cannot expect much business expansion with its current domestic operations alone."
Hironobu Sawaki, analyst at Nikko Research Centre, said the cancellation could have a negative impact on Sega's share prices, while the impact would be neutral for Bandai.
"Sega would have acquired much-wanted distribution routes for children's goods and Bandai's sales know-how," he said.
On Tuesday, both companies' shares fell, with Sega sliding 20 yen to close at 3,700 yen and Bandai dropping 30 yen to end at 2,760 yen.
Many analysts noted, however, that even if the two firms merged as planned, business prospects would be shaky as each firm has its own individual problems.

"Not many had thought that the merger would boost profits in the future," said Hiroyuki Ono, an analyst at Nomura Research Institute. He predicted that the merger's cancellation would not have a detrimental impact on the firms' business.
Sega's 32-bit video game machine Saturn is losing money and is unlikely to turn profitable in the future, analysts said.

In December, Sega lowered its earnings forecast for fiscal year 1996/97, which ended on March 31, as it liquidated its inventory of 16-bit products and wrote off accumulated losses at its U.S. unit. It forecast a parent net profit of 5.3 billion yen ($45.6 million) in 1996/97.

Bandai, for its part, is burdened by extremely weak sales of its Pippin Atmark machines, a video game player with Internet capabilities. Bandai has stopped producing the multimedia terminal, although sales will continue.

Bandai is now profiting, however, from the runaway success of its "Tamagotchi" virtual pet toy that features an electronic bird. The toy became an instant hit after its debut in November, with about five million units already shipped.

Despite brisk sales of the "Tamagotchi," Bandai had to lower its group earnings forecast for 1996/97 in January. It predicted a group net loss of 9 billion yen ($77.5 million) in 1996/97, against a net profit of 10.4 billion yen ($89.6 million) in 1995/96.
The two firms are due to announce earnings results on Wednesday for fiscal year 1996/97. ($=116 yen)
